newsitem.title: KENYA: Eight civilians killed in Rwanda-aid workers.
newsitem.headline: Eight civilians killed in Rwanda-aid workers.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen shot and killed at least eight civilians including a child in an ambush near the Rwandan capital on Sunday, aid workers said on Monday.

Speaking by telephone from Kigali to Nairobi, they quoted women survivors as saying the gunmen wore shabby military-style clothes, indicating that they might be Hutu former troops or militiamen blamed for a series of attacks in the northwest.
State-run Rwanda radio said unidentified attackers killed several people on Sunday when they ambushed two mini-buses on the main road between the capital and the northwest town of Ruhengeri.
It said gunmen separated members of the Tutsi minority from members of the Hutu majority in the first mini-bus and then killed the Tutsis and set fire to the second vehicle, killing several people.
There was no comment available from Rwandan officials.
"Our convoy was the first to come across the ambush site at Shyorongi, 25 km (12 miles) northwest of Kigali," Jake Fortney of the Adventist Development Relief Agency (ADRA), told Reuters.
"Women running from the ambush told us three vehicles, two mini-buses and a pickup, were blocked by a log across the road.

"The women said men were ordered to lie down on the road and were shot. My driver saw seven dead men and one (dead) child. The women all ran away," said Fortney, adding ADRA vehicles took three wounded women to a hospital near the town of Ruhengeri.
He said one of the two ambushed mini-buses was set ablaze.
It was the nearest ambush to Kigali since a wave of attacks began last month in the northwestern prefecture of Ruhengeri and the west blamed by the government on former Hutu troops and militiamen.
Gunmen killed four U.N. human rights monitors -- a Briton, a Cambodian and two Rwandans -- in an ambush last Tuesday in southwestern Rwanda. Their Rwandan driver later died of his wounds.
Three Spanish aid workers were killed in Ruhengeri town on January 18.
A 61-year-old Canadian missionary was shot dead on February 2 in Ruhengeri prefecture -- although there were doubts among diplomats that his attacker was a Hutu former soldier or militiaman.
Rwanda's government says the attacks are mounted by former Hutu troops and Interahamwe militiamen who returned home from Zaire and Tanzania among more than a million refugees late last year.
The army has said it will hunt down the Hutu killers, who were involved in the 1994 genocide of some 800,000 people.
